title: Unit Testing
summary: Writing automated tests with xUnit - test projects, Facts and Theories with InlineData, Arrange-Act-Assert, asserting values, collections and exceptions, testing async code, fakes for dependencies, what makes code testable, test naming, and how a test framework finds and runs tests with attributes and reflection.

cards.q: What is the difference between [Fact] and [Theory]?
cards.a:
A Fact is one test without parameters; a Theory runs once for each InlineData set

A Theory is a parameterised test: each `[InlineData(...)]` line gives one set of arguments and one test run.

cards.q: Why does an InvoiceService that takes an IClock test more easily than one that reads DateTime.Now?
cards.a:
A test can give it a fixed clock, so the due date is the same on every run

With `DateTime.Now` the expected due date changes every day. A fixed clock makes the result predictable.

cards.q: xUnit creates a new instance of the test class for each test. What does that guarantee?
cards.a:
Tests cannot affect each other through instance fields

A fresh object per test keeps tests independent. Static state is still shared, which is one more reason to avoid it.
